newsitem.title: UK: Britain to veto EU beef labelling - paper.
newsitem.headline: Britain to veto EU beef labelling - paper.

text.p: Britain will block a European Union proposal to label all beef with its country of origin, fearing a conspiracy to undermine British beef sales, the Financial Times said on Saturday.
The paper said the government fears that continental European consumers would not buy beef labelled as British even after the worldwide ban on exports is lifted.

The newspaper said that when farm ministers meet on Monday, British Agriculture Minister Douglas Hogg intends to oppose EU Commission plans to label all beef in the EU with information about where the animal was born, reared and slaughtered.
It added that British opposition will scupper the plans, which require backing from all 15 EU ministers., and that Britain expects support from Ireland, Denmark and Italy.

"We think the motive for supporting the proposal is protectionist. The signal being sent is that meat from country A is OK, just don't buy the British stuff," the newspaper quoted an unnamed British official as saying.
It said Britain favours a voluntary regime, while the Commission argues that a compulsory system is vital to regain consumer confidence following the Mad Cow crisis.
There was no immediate comment available from British officials on the Financial Times report.
